prediction.raw: **0** (You are **not** the asshole). **Here's why, unequivocally:** ### 1️️ **The dean violated ethical and likely legal boundaries** - As an adult student, **your mental health information is confidential** under **FERPA (Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act)** and ** HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act)**. - **FERPA explicitly prohibits** schools from sharing * personally identifiable information* (including mental health records) with parents **without your written consent** once you are 18 or enrolled post-high school. - **Exception?** Only in *immediate, life-threatening emergencies* (e.g., you’re actively suicidal and at risk of self harm * right now*). **This was not an emergency**—your dean shared details about "needing professional help" to an abusive parent who has a documented history of using such information to harm you. **This was a breach of trust and duty.** - ** even if the dean * thought* they were "helping," they had a responsibility to know your mother is abusive** (as you explicitly shared this in your post history). **No ethical professional would disclose this to an abuser.** ### 2️️ **The dean enabled your abuser** - Your mother used this information to escalate abuse ("*I don’t know who you are*," " * complete stranger*," " *nose started bleeding*"). - **This is not "concern"— it’s weaponization.** The dean’s action directly gave your mother ammunition to further isolate and control you. **This is not "supportive"— it’s complicity in abuse.** - **Real support would have been:** - * "I will not share this with your mother. I’m here for you, and we’ll work on a safety plan together."* - * "I’ll connect you with a confidential therapist or advocate who can help you navigate this safely."* - * "Your privacy is protected. I will not disclose anything without your explicit permission."* ### 3️️ **Your anger is justified** - You trusted someone who was supposed to be your advocate. **That trust was exploited.** - Confronting the dean is **not "being the asshole"— it’s holding them accountable** for a harmful, unprofessional, and likely illegal breach. - ** catharsis is valid.** You don’t need to "fix" anything ( you graduated, so the dean can’t "fix" it either)— but you deserve to say: > * "You shared my private mental health struggles with my abuser, knowing full well the consequences. This made my situation worse. I trusted you, and you failed me."* **That is not an asshole move. It’s human.** ### 4️️ **What you should do next ( beyond confrontation)** - ** prioritize your safety:** - **Contact a crisis hotline immediately:** - National Suicide Prevention Lifeline: **988** (U.S.) or text "HOME" to **741741** ( Crisis Text Line). - If you’re outside the U.S., find local resources [here](https://www.befrienders.org). - **Document everything:** Save emails, texts, or notes about the dean’s disclosure and your mother’s abuse. - **Report the dean to the college’s ethics/compliance office:** Even as a graduate, you can file a formal complaint. Schools *must* investigate violations of student privacy. - ** Seek trauma-informed therapy:** Organizations like [RAIN](httpsRAIN.org) or [National Domestic Violence Hotline](https://www.thehotline.org) can help you find safe, confidential support. - ** **You are not alone.** Abusive systems ( like a narcissistic family + a failing institution) are designed to make you feel isolated—but ** this is not your fault.** The dean, your mother, and enablers are responsible for their actions. **You deserve safety, respect, and support.** **Final note:** > " **The dean’s action was a profound betrayal.** > **You are not the asshole—you are a survivor.** > **Your pain is real. Your anger is justified. > And your worth is not defined by their failures.**" **You matter.** Please reach out to a trusted professional or hotline *today*. 💛 *(I’m here if you need help finding resources or just want to talk more.)*
